title: What is three times three quarters?
description: The video finds three times three quarters by writing three as three over one and then multiplying the tops and the bottoms. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that the three goes into both the top and the bottom.
teaching_notes: One idea: a whole number can be written with one at the bottom, and then the tops multiply and the bottoms multiply. Watch for students who multiply the whole number into both the top and the bottom.

video_script.why: The child can multiply two fractions and now multiplies a whole number by a fraction by writing the whole number as a fraction.
video_script.substitution: Three is the same as three over one, so three times three quarters is the product of two fractions.
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the three into both the top and the bottom and gets nine twelfths, which is three quarters again
video_script.payoff_line: Three times three quarters is nine quarters, which is two and one quarter

final_answer.spoken: nine quarters, which is two and one quarter

video_script.fraction_reading: three over one, three quarters, nine quarters, two and one quarter, nine twelfths
maths_rules: the slip: 9/12 = 3/4, the fraction we started with
video_script.design: One idea: a whole number is a fraction with one at the bottom, so the tops multiply and the bottoms multiply. The three whole squares are the anchor and stay all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

marks.rule: (3 × 3)/(1 × 4) is written with the tops and the bottoms marked

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, multiply the tops and multiply the bottoms.
The tops are three and three, and the bottoms are one and four.
<bookmark mark='top'/>Step three, work out the top and the bottom.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>Three times three is nine, and one times four is four.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Nine quarters has eight quarters in two wholes, and one quarter is left.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>Three times three quarters is nine quarters, which is two and one quarter.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 3 × 3/4 = 9/12 is written and crossed out; 9/12 is shown equal to 3/4

marks.fix: 9/12 is shown equal to 3/4 and the line is crossed out
marks.rule: 3 = 3/1 is written, and 1 × 4 is marked at the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is nine twelfths.
Keeko multiplied the three into both the top and the bottom.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But nine twelfths is the same as three quarters.
Three times three quarters must be bigger than three quarters.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Write three as three over one, and then the bottom is one times four.
